title: Even or Odd
statement: Write a program that takes an integer as input and prints whether it is even or odd.

title: Leap Year Checker
statement: Given a year, determine if it is a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except for century years which must be divisible by 400.

title: Grade Calculator
statement: Write a program that accepts a student's score (0-100) and prints the grade: A (90-100), B (80-89), C (70-79), D (60-69), F (below 60).

title: Simple Calculator
statement: Build a calculator that takes two numbers and an operator (+, -, *, /) and prints the result. Handle division by zero gracefully.

title: Multiplication Table
statement: Print the multiplication table of a given number from 1 to 10.

title: Sum of N Natural Numbers
statement: Write a program to calculate the sum of the first N natural numbers using a loop.

title: Star Pattern — Right Triangle
statement:
Print a right-angled triangle pattern of stars with N rows.
Row 1 has 1 star, row 2 has 2 stars, and so on.

title: FizzBuzz
statement: Print numbers from 1 to N. For multiples of 3 print 'Fizz', for multiples of 5 print 'Buzz', and for multiples of both print 'FizzBuzz'.
example_output:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz

title: Count Vowels
statement: Write a program that counts the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a given string. Consider both uppercase and lowercase.

title: Reverse a String
statement: Write a program that takes a string and prints it in reverse order.

title: Palindrome Check
statement: Check if a given string is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Ignore case and spaces.

title: Count Words in a String
statement: Count the number of words in a given sentence. Words are separated by spaces.

title: Anagram Checker
statement: Given two strings, check if they are anagrams of each other (contain the same characters in a different order). Ignore case and spaces.

title: Find Maximum in a List
statement: Write a program that finds the maximum element in a list of integers without using the built-in max() function.

title: Remove Duplicates
statement: Given a list of integers, remove all duplicate elements and return the list with unique elements only, preserving original order.

title: Rotate a List
statement: Rotate a list to the right by K positions. The last K elements should move to the front.

title: Two Sum
statement: Given a list of integers and a target sum, find two numbers in the list that add up to the target. Return their indices.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
statement: Given two sorted lists, merge them into a single sorted list without using any built-in sort function.

title: Word Frequency Counter
statement: Given a sentence, count the frequency of each word and display the result as key-value pairs. Ignore case.

title: Character Frequency
statement: Count the frequency of each character in a string (ignore spaces) and return the result as a dictionary.

title: Group Anagrams
statement: Given a list of strings, group anagrams together. Two strings are anagrams if they contain the same characters in any order.

title: Temperature Converter Function
statement: Write a function that converts temperature between Celsius and Fahrenheit. The function should accept the temperature value and the unit to convert to.

title: Recursive Factorial
statement: Write a recursive function to calculate the factorial of a non-negative integer N. Handle the base case (0! = 1).

title: Power Function
statement: Implement a function power(base, exponent) that calculates base raised to the exponent without using the ** operator or pow(). Handle negative exponents.

title: Prime Number Checker
statement: Write a function that checks if a given number is a prime number. Return True if prime, False otherwise.

title: GCD of Two Numbers
statement: Find the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of two positive integers using the Euclidean algorithm.

title: Fibonacci Sequence
statement: Generate the first N numbers of the Fibonacci sequence. The sequence starts with 0 and 1, and each subsequent number is the sum of the previous two.

title: Sum of Digits
statement: Write a program that calculates the sum of digits of a given positive integer.

title: Armstrong Number
statement: Check if a number is an Armstrong number. An Armstrong number of N digits is one where the sum of each digit raised to the power N equals the number itself.

title: Linear Search
statement: Implement linear search: given a list and a target value, return the index of the target if found, or -1 if not found.

title: Binary Search
statement: Implement binary search on a sorted list. Return the index of the target element, or -1 if not found. The list is guaranteed to be sorted in ascending order.

title: Bubble Sort
statement: Implement the bubble sort algorithm to sort a list of integers in ascending order. Show or return the sorted list.

title: Selection Sort
statement: Implement selection sort: repeatedly find the minimum element from the unsorted part and place it at the beginning.

title: Insertion Sort
statement: Implement insertion sort: build the sorted list one element at a time by inserting each element into its correct position.

title: Count Sort Frequency
statement: Given a list of integers in the range 0 to K, implement counting sort. Count the occurrences of each integer and reconstruct the sorted list.

title: Two Sum
statement: Given an array of integers and a target sum, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to the target. Assume each input has exactly one solution.

title: Merge Sorted Arrays
statement: Given two sorted integer arrays, merge them into a single sorted array without using built-in sort functions.

title: Find Missing Number
statement: Given an array containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], find the one number in the range that is missing from the array.

title: Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. Open brackets must be closed by the same type in the correct order.

title: Reverse String Using Stack
statement: Use a stack data structure to reverse an input string. Do not use built-in string reverse slicing.

title: Implement Queue using Two Stacks
statement: Implement a first-in-first-out (FIFO) queue using only two standard stacks. Support push, pop, and peek operations.

title: Next Greater Element
statement: Given an array of integers, find the next greater element for every element. If no greater element exists to its right, output -1.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix). Valid operators are +, -, *, /.

title: Power Function (x^n)
statement: Implement a recursive function to calculate x raised to the power n (where n is a non-negative integer) in O(log n) time.

title: Tower of Hanoi
statement: Write a recursive function to print the moves required to transfer N disks from rod A to rod C using helper rod B, following standard Hanoi rules.
example_output:
Move disk 1 from A to C
Move disk 2 from A to B
Move disk 1 from C to B
Move disk 3 from A to C...

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, find its maximum depth (the number of nodes along the longest path from the root down to the farthest leaf node).

title: Invert Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree (swap left and right child nodes recursively) and return its root.

title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the inorder traversal of its nodes' values (Left -> Root -> Right).

title: Lowest Common Ancestor in BST
statement: Given a Binary Search Tree (BST) and two node values, find their Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA).
